title: Parents and in-laws
hookLine: honoring elders while building a new home
tomorrow: three generations, one evening. can a living room be a sangat?

lines: A MORTAR AND PESTLE, NOT A TALK.
NOT ONE WORD ABOUT THE FIGHT.
cards: Crushed cardamom. Ginger hitting hot water. The sharp sweet smell of milk about to boil over.

That's what Jasleen smells when she walks back into her in-laws' kitchen, braced for a talk. Instead, Aman's mother hands her a mortar and pestle and says, crush the cardamom, I'll show you how Aman likes it.
She lets the tea rise to the rim and fall back, again and again, and doesn't say one word about the fight. Aman, in the doorway, looks like he's been up all night.

teach.h: BHAI JETHA, BIBI BHANI, GURU AMAR DAS.
teach.b: Sikh history has a son-in-law in it who is easy to miss. Bhai Jetha married Bibi Bhani, the daughter of Guru Amar Das, and lived and served in the household and sangat of his father-in-law.

Tradition says he carried loads, cooked and served in the langar with such humility that the Guru chose him as the next Guru. He became Guru Ram Das, the one who wrote the lavan Jasleen walked a week ago.
And tradition remembers Bibi Bhani for serving her father too, with the same care. So the tradition holds two things at once.

teach.h: HONOR ELDERS; BUILD A NEW HOME.
teach.b: Honor the elders: the parents who raised you, and the ones you married into, with respect and service. And build a new home, with its own way of doing things. Those two don't cancel out.
They meet in kitchens. Honoring isn't obeying in everything, and building isn't walking away. It's the tea made the way Aman's mother makes it, and, by next month, Jasleen's dal on the same stove.
Aman's mother pours three cups. She hands the first one to Jasleen, not to her son. That's the whole talk.

how: In some Sikh families, newly married couples live near or with parents for a time; elders are honored with respect and service, and the couple gradually shapes a home of their own.

games.q: your new in-laws fold the laundry a way that makes no sense to you, and they've just refolded yours. what does today's lesson suggest?
o: learn their way with respect, and keep a few ways that are yours.
refold it your way in front of them, so the rules are clear.
go along with every way they do things, for good.
games.why: honor the elders and build a new home: honoring isn't obeying in everything, and building isn't walking away.

practice: If you have a cup of tea, coffee or even water nearby, hold it and breathe in its smell before you sip, slowly. Let the taste bring to mind one elder, yours or someone else's, who made something like it for you.
Hold the warmth in both hands, and stay with that person for the sit.

carryVoice: Honor the elders, and let the tea rise and fall back as many times as it takes. Day done, cup in hand.
